regions.name: Middle East
overview: The US–Iran confrontation remains on a war footing despite mediation. US projectiles hit Qeshm Island again around 6–8 November, which Trump called 'minor strikes'. UKMTO counted at least 11 ships attacked in and around Hormuz in the week to 6 November, three of which sank. Attacks continued on 7 and 10 November, including on an ADNOC vessel inside UAE territorial waters. The IRGC says its 2,000 km missile-range limit no longer applies, and Mojtaba Khamenei has reportedly ordered an unrestrained response to any new attack. Araghchi lobbied 12 foreign ministers in 48 hours, but the mediators have little to show, and analysts see the pendulum leaning toward conflict.

The Yemen–Saudi war is intensifying and drawing in regional partners. A strike on the al-Hadara market in Taiz on 6 November killed at least 20–30 people; the Houthis blamed Saudi Arabia, and the government blamed a Houthi missile. The Houthis claimed hits on Riyadh's airport, its financial district and Abqaiq on 8 and 10 November. Saudi Arabia confirmed minor damage to an Aramco office in Riyadh and multiple interceptions over Riyadh and the Eastern Province. Syria signed a defence pact with Riyadh and says about 600 special forces will deploy to the kingdom. OCHA counts more than 323,000 people displaced in Yemen since August.

Israel has moved toward a change of government. Herzog gave Gadi Eisenkot the mandate on 8 November with 67 recommendations, against 46 for Netanyahu, and he now has 28 days plus a possible 14-day extension. Netanyahu stays on as caretaker in the meantime. Lethal Israeli fire continues in Gaza: four were killed on 5 November and at least four on 10 November, and the Health Ministry's post-ceasefire toll has passed 1,600. In the West Bank, a 14-year-old was killed in Burqa around 10 November amid record settler violence. In Lebanon, Israeli strikes and shelling continued in the south (Bint Jbeil, Qantara, al-Mansouri), with no confirmed deaths after 4 November.

Jordan suffered a second deadly terrorist attack in two weeks: a released ISIS-linked convict killed a police officer near the Sri Lankan embassy in Amman on 5 November, prompting nationwide raids. Iran struck Kurdish opposition sites in Iraqi Kurdistan with drones on 4 November, and an explosive drone was found in Kirkuk on 6 November. Israeli incursions in Quneitra and Daraa continued at a high rate, with more than 60 violations recorded from 1 to 5 November. North Africa was calm: Egypt reopened its Tripoli embassy after 12 years, Libya's UN-led 4+4 election track continues, and no new incidents were found for Tunisia.

countries.name: Gaza
incidents: 5 Nov — Deir el-Balah / az-Zawayda / Bureij / Khan Younis: Israeli drone strikes and gunfire killed at least four people, including a man in a displacement tent and a child in Bureij, according to medical sources; the Health Ministry's post-ceasefire toll reached 1,602 killed.
6 Nov — Khan Younis: A teenager was killed by Israeli fire; other reports put the day's toll across Gaza at five, including a 12-year-old boy and a woman.
10 Nov — Gaza City: Two Israeli air strikes killed three people, including a child, according to Palestinian medical authorities cited by Reuters.
10 Nov — Khan Younis (coast and town): Israeli forces shot two people, killing one, and the Israeli navy fired on fishing boats, wounding a fisherman and damaging two boats.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Israeli drone strikes, air strikes, gunfire and naval fire kill people almost every day under the nominal ceasefire. The post-ceasefire toll passed 1,600 on 5 November, and the Gaza Media Office counted 753 violations in October alone. Israeli forces keep demolishing homes and moving the Yellow Line east of Khan Younis and Deir el-Balah. Politically, Eisenkot now holds the mandate to form a government. Whether he succeeds or not, no new Israeli government is likely to change Gaza policy before mid-December, and any shift toward phase two of the ceasefire would come in early 2027 at the earliest. Over the next 90 days, expect continued lethal strikes at a rate of several deaths a day, further land seizure behind the Yellow Line, crossings opened and closed as leverage, and a severe winter shelter crisis. A renewed US/Israel–Iran war would cut aid access and attention further.

events.place: Deir el-Balah / az-Zawayda / Bureij / Khan Younis

forecasts.statement: The Gaza Ministry of Health reports that 1,800 or more Palestinians have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if a Gaza Health Ministry figure, as reported by Al Jazeera, Reuters, AP or OCHA, published on or before 2027-01-31, gives a post-ceasefire death toll of at least 1,800.

countries.name: Lebanon
incidents: 4 Nov — Qabrikha (Marjayoun district): An Israeli drone strike on a motorcycle killed one person and wounded another, according to the Health Ministry. Israel said it targeted Hezbollah members; residents said both were Amal-affiliated rescue workers. The ministry's toll since 2 March stands at 4,390 killed.
6 Nov — Bint Jbeil: Israeli air strike reported by Lebanese state media; no casualty figures were given.
7 Nov — Bani Hayyan / Zawtar al-Sharqiyeh: Israeli forces carried out a detonation in Bani Hayyan and shelled Zawtar al-Sharqiyeh, according to Lebanese media.
10 Nov — Qantara / al-Mansouri / Majdal Zoun: An Israeli air strike hit Qantara, and artillery fire hit around al-Mansouri and Majdal Zoun, according to Lebanese state media.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Israel occupies and holds a security zone in the south and strikes, shells and demolishes property there several times a week. The Qabrikha strike on 4 November, outside the zone, shows that lethal fire continues even though no deaths were confirmed between 5 and 12 November. Lebanon–Israel talks continue, and the Amal-linked victims at Qabrikha were read locally as a pressure signal. Over the next 90 days, the dominant risk remains Hezbollah being drawn into a renewed US/Israel–Iran war. Iran's declared 'unrestrained response' doctrine raises that risk, and an Israeli air campaign on the Dahiyeh and the Bekaa would very probably follow. Without that trigger, expect continued drone strikes on individuals, artillery fire and village demolitions in the south, state–Hezbollah friction over disarmament, and a growing security gap as UNIFIL's mandate ends on 31 December. An Eisenkot-led government would not quickly change Israel's posture in the north.

forecasts.statement: Israel carries out an air strike on Beirut's southern suburbs (Dahiyeh).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera or L'Orient Today report an Israeli air or drone strike hitting Beirut's southern suburbs between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

countries.name: Iran
incidents: 6 Nov — Qeshm Island: US strikes hit the island with two projectiles, part of a weeks-long series against Iranian air defences and launchers; Trump called them 'minor strikes'. Iranian state media reported further US projectiles and explosions on Qeshm on 8 Nov.

1–6 Nov — Strait of Hormuz: UKMTO recorded at least 11 ships attacked in and around the strait, three of which sank. The IRGC and Iran's army claimed to have downed a US MQ-1 (6 Nov) and an MQ-9 (7 Nov).

7 Nov — Off Khasab (Musandam): A tanker caught fire and its crew evacuated, and UKMTO later reclassified the incident as an attack; Iran's navy claimed a tanker running without a transponder hit a mine.

10 Nov — Off Limah (Oman) / UAE waters: UKMTO said a tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile 19 nm north-east of Limah (crew safe), and ADNOC said one of its vessels was damaged in an attack in UAE territorial waters; the IRGC claimed two tankers caught fire using an unauthorised route.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Iran is under repeated, if limited, US strikes on its territory around Hormuz, including on Qeshm on 6 and 8 November. Its campaign against shipping continues and is spreading: three ships sank in one week, and a vessel was hit inside UAE waters. Drone shoot-downs are claimed almost weekly. Tehran is hardening its stance. The IRGC says the 2,000 km missile-range limit no longer applies and talks openly of a nuclear-doctrine change, and the Supreme Leader has reportedly ordered an unrestrained response to any new attack. Diplomacy is running in parallel: Araghchi met 12 foreign ministers, Rezaei met Putin, and Qatar and Oman are mediating. US analysts see the post-midterm reshuffle as raising the short-term risk of war. Over the next 90 days, the most likely path is continued tit-for-tat at Hormuz without a full air campaign. A wider US (and possibly Israeli) strike campaign on mainland targets remains a realistic possibility, and it would bring Iranian missile fire at Israel and at Gulf and Jordanian bases. A framework deal on 'Hormuz first' is possible but unlikely before February.

forecasts.statement: The United States and/or Israel strike targets on the Iranian mainland away from the Hormuz coast and islands (e.g. Tehran, Isfahan, Natanz, Fordow, or other inland sites).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP or Al Jazeera report a US or Israeli strike on a site in an inland Iranian province (not Hormozgan, Bushehr coast or the Gulf islands) between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

forecasts.statement: The United States and Iran publicly announce an agreement or framework to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if both governments, or the mediating state (Qatar/Oman) with both sides confirming, announce an agreed arrangement for reopening Hormuz, as reported by Reuters or AP, by 2027-01-31.

countries.name: Yemen
incidents: 6 Nov — al-Hadara market, al-Waziyah (Taiz province): A strike on a vegetable market killed at least 20–30 people according to Houthi officials (22 killed and 30 injured in another count). The Houthis blamed Saudi F-15s; the government blamed a Houthi ballistic missile, and AP could not verify either account.

6 Nov — Taiz fronts: Government forces claimed to have retaken al-Nidani, Shaab al-Sarari, parts of Sanamat and Ribat al-Qarn; OCHA reports more than 323,000 people displaced since August, and about 800,000 people in Taiz are cut off from supplies.
8 Nov — Saada / Sanaa: The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed two ballistic missile launchers in Saada and one in Sanaa used against Riyadh and the Eastern Province.

10 Nov — Sanaa / Hodeidah / Saada: Coalition air strikes hit the state oil company in Sanaa, wounding six according to Houthi-affiliated media, with further strikes on Hodeidah and Saada; on 9 Nov government forces reported advances in Lahj.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Full-scale war continues on the Taiz, Lahj, Marib and al-Jawf fronts. The government's 'Dawn of Yemen' offensive claims steady gains (unverified), while the Houthis keep Taiz under siege and fire missiles at Saudi Arabia almost daily. Coalition air strikes are hitting Houthi launchers and oil infrastructure in Sanaa, Saada and Hodeidah. The 6 November Taiz market massacre, whose attribution is disputed, shows the rising civilian cost: the UN counts 281 civilian casualties since August, and displacement is above 323,000. The arrival of Syrian special forces in Saudi Arabia and Egypt's pledged support widen the coalition. Over the next 90 days, expect continued ground fighting without a decisive collapse of either side, more strikes on fuel and port infrastructure, a serious risk of mass deaths in Taiz if the siege holds, and possible Houthi moves against Red Sea shipping if US–Iran fighting escalates.

forecasts.statement: Yemeni government forces open a land route into Taiz city, breaking the Houthi siege.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera or OCHA report that government forces have reopened a road into Taiz city allowing civilian or aid traffic, by 2027-02-12.

countries.name: Israel
incidents: 8 Nov — Jerusalem: President Herzog gave Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government after 67 MKs recommended him against 46 for Netanyahu; he has 28 days, extendable by 14.
6 Nov — Duma / Burin (south of Nablus, West Bank): Settlers burned tents in Duma and cut power lines in Burin.

10 Nov — Burqa (near Nablus, West Bank): Israeli forces killed 14-year-old Moataz Iyad Daghlas during a raid and wounded two other young men; the army said soldiers fired to stop stone-throwing at vehicles.
10 Nov — Near Nablus (West Bank): Settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives, injuring a photojournalist.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. No missile, drone or rocket attacks on Israeli territory were found this week. West Bank violence (raids, a teenager killed, record settler attacks) is serious but does not amount to hostilities on Israel's own territory. The risk of escalation stays high: Iran says nothing is now 'off limits' and that any new attack will meet an unrestrained response. A renewed US or Israeli campaign against Iran would very likely bring Iranian missile fire, and possibly Hezbollah and Houthi attacks, which would move Israel to CRITICAL. Politically, Eisenkot's mandate and his 67 recommendations make a change of government possible. However, depending on the Arab parties makes a stable coalition hard to assemble, and a repeat election in early 2027 remains plausible. Netanyahu's caretaker government runs security policy until a new cabinet is sworn in. Expect continued West Bank raids and settler violence during the olive harvest, isolated Palestinian attacks, and sharp polarisation over the Arab parties' role.

forecasts.statement: A new Israeli government headed by Gadi Eisenkot wins a Knesset confidence vote and is sworn in.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Times of Israel, Haaretz, Reuters or AP report that the Knesset approved a government with Eisenkot as prime minister by 2027-01-15.

countries.name: Iraq
incidents: 4 Nov — Balisan valley (north-east of Erbil) / Halabja: Iranian drones struck a Komala headquarters and a house in Halabja province, causing property damage; no casualties were reported at Halabja.
5 Nov — Kirkuk: The Counter-Terrorism Service detained an Islamic State suspect amid concern over ISIS sleeper cells in Kirkuk and Garmian.
6 Nov — Kirkuk: The National Security Service found an explosive-laden drone and destroyed it in a controlled detonation; its origin was not established.
5 Nov — Baghdad: Trump spoke with Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi about regional security, and US envoy Tom Barrack visited Baghdad.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Iraq faces recurring cross-border Iranian drone strikes on Kurdish opposition groups (more than 1,000 since the start of the conflict, per the Long War Journal) and an explosive drone found in Kirkuk. ISIS has stepped up activity in the Hawija–Kirkuk belt since the US-led coalition left on 30 September. Iran-aligned factions continue to resist disarmament. No lethal attacks were confirmed this week, but the underlying threat has not decreased. Over the next 90 days, the main risk is a renewed US–Iran war: militia drone and rocket attacks on US diplomatic sites and Gulf neighbours, and US strikes on PMF positions as seen earlier in 2026, would then become likely. Expect continued ISIS hit-and-run attacks and curfews in Kirkuk, more Iranian strikes in the Kurdistan Region, and political strain in the KRG after the PUK left the cabinet.

forecasts.statement: A drone or rocket attack targets the US Embassy in Baghdad or the US consulate in Erbil.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, Shafaq News or Rudaw report a drone or rocket attack aimed at (including intercepted over) the US Embassy in Baghdad or the US consulate in Erbil between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
incidents: 8 Nov — Riyadh / Eastern Province: The coalition said air defences intercepted ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh and the Eastern Province (counts vary from three to five missiles plus a drone), after loud explosions were heard in the capital.

8 Nov — Riyadh (financial district): The Ministry of Energy said an Aramco administrative building was hit in an attempted attack, causing minor damage and no casualties; the Houthis claimed hits on King Khalid airport, Aramco storage and Abqaiq.

10 Nov — Riyadh / Abqaiq: Saudi forces intercepted two Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh; the Houthis claimed strikes on King Khalid airport, the financial district, pipeline pumping stations and Aramco infrastructure at Abqaiq (unverified).
8 Nov — Riyadh: A Syrian official told AP that about 600 Syrian special forces will deploy to Saudi Arabia within a week, following the 5 Nov Saudi–Syrian defence cooperation agreement.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained after a strict re-test against the definitions. Saudi territory is under direct military attack almost daily, with ballistic missiles and drones fired at Riyadh, the Eastern Province, Najran and Jizan. These attacks hit an Aramco building in the capital on 8 November, and similar attacks killed 13 at King Khalid airport and two at Dammam airport in October. The kingdom is also an active party to a war, striking Houthi launchers and infrastructure inside Yemen. This is direct military attack on the country on a weekly basis, not proximity to a war. Riyadh is expanding its coalition with Syrian special forces, Egyptian support, French protection for Yanbu and UK fighter jets. Over the next 90 days, expect continued salvos on Riyadh and energy sites in the Eastern Province, interception debris and periodic civilian casualties, flight disruption, and more attacks on Gulf shipping. A renewed US–Iran war would raise the threat to Gulf energy infrastructure; a US–Iran deal could over time weaken Iranian backing for the Houthi campaign.

forecasts.statement: A single Houthi missile or drone attack on Saudi territory kills five or more people.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Saudi authorities, Reuters, AP or Al Jazeera report at least five deaths from one Houthi attack (including interception debris) on Saudi territory between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

countries.name: Syria
incidents: 1–5 Nov — Quneitra / western Daraa: The Sijil Center recorded at least 66 Israeli violations, including incursions, checkpoints, home raids, detentions of olive pickers in Wadi Kuya, and artillery shells near al-Mantara Dam; no casualties were reported.
6 Nov — al-Samdaniyah al-Sharqiyah (Quneitra countryside): Israeli forces fired artillery at the village, according to Syrian state media.
5 Nov — Aleppo: Authorities dismantled an ISIS cell they said was linked to a series of attacks and assassinations in the province.

8 Nov — Damascus: Syria confirmed it will send about 600 special forces to Saudi Arabia to support the fight against the Houthis, after al-Sharaa and MBS signed a defence cooperation agreement on 5 Nov.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Foreign forces continue to hold and operate on Syrian territory: Israeli troops patrol, set up checkpoints, raid homes and fire artillery in Quneitra and western Daraa at more than ten incidents a day. Suwayda remains outside state control, and ACLED data show ISIS attacks on government forces more than tripling in 2026. Two officers were killed near Damascus on 22 October. No deaths were confirmed this week, but the conditions behind CRITICAL (loss of control over territory and foreign military operations on Syrian soil) have not eased. Damascus is now exporting forces to Saudi Arabia, which ties Syria directly to the Yemen war and could make it a Houthi or Iranian target. Over the next 90 days, expect continued Israeli incursions and detentions with occasional killings, ISIS attacks and government raids from Aleppo to Deir ez-Zor, and possible Jordanian strikes in the south. A security deal with Israel is unlikely before a new Israeli government forms.

countries.name: Egypt
incidents: 8 Nov — Tripoli (Libya): Egypt reopened its embassy in Tripoli after a 12-year closure, with Foreign Minister Abdelatty attending.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. No security incidents on Egyptian soil were found this week. Egypt's exposure is regional. Cairo has authorised military support to Saudi Arabia, which Sisi limits to defending Saudi territory, and the Houthis call this a 'declaration of war'. Syria's troop deployment and France's and the UK's commitments make an Egyptian air-defence or naval contribution more likely to become visible. Reopening the Tripoli embassy signals a more active Libya policy alongside friction with the Haftar family. Over the next 90 days, the key indicators are the announcement of any Egyptian deployment, Houthi threats or attacks on Egyptian forces or Suez-bound shipping, Sinai security, and further pressure from closures of the Rafah crossing. HIGH would apply if Egyptian forces come under direct attack, if the Houthis target Suez traffic, or if a significant terrorist attack takes place in Sinai.

countries.name: Jordan
incidents: 5 Nov — Amman (near the Sri Lankan embassy): A stabbing attack on a security post killed one officer and wounded another. The suspect, an ISIS-linked convict recently released after a 2020 terrorism case, was arrested; authorities called it a planned 'terrorist attack'.
5–6 Nov — Karak / Irbid / Marka / Zarqa: Security agencies carried out sweeping overnight raids across several governorates after the Amman attack.

3 Nov — Amman: Prosecutors charged three suspects in the 23 Oct Karak church attack (nine killed, about 40 wounded) with terrorism offences carrying the death penalty and referred the case to the State Security Court.
9 Nov — Eastern border: The Eastern Military Zone foiled an attempt to smuggle a large quantity of narcotics using guided balloons.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained after a strict re-test. The level is justified by events inside Jordan, not by proximity to the regional wars. Two lethal terrorist attacks in under two weeks (the Karak church massacre on 23 October and the killing of a police officer in Amman on 5 November) meet the definition of recurring lethal violence by terrorist actors. Both involved recently released militants, and ISIS communications with the Karak cell reportedly included a list of targets, which points to a live network risk rather than isolated incidents. It is not CRITICAL, because there is no sustained armed conflict and no loss of territorial control. Over the next 90 days, expect continued raids and arrests, a State Security Court trial in the Karak case, scrutiny of the release of terrorism convicts, possible further strikes in southern Syria, and steady drug and weapons smuggling from Syria. A renewed US–Iran war would very likely bring missile and drone fire at US-used bases in Jordan, which would justify CRITICAL. A quiet month without new attacks would justify MODERATE.

forecasts.statement: Another attack inside Jordan that authorities describe as terrorist kills at least one person.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Jordanian authorities (Public Security Directorate/Petra), as reported by Reuters, AP, The National or Asharq Al-Awsat, attribute a fatal attack on Jordanian territory to terrorism between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

countries.name: Libya
incidents: 4 Nov — Eastern Libya: Niger signed a memorandum of understanding with Khalifa Haftar's command to expand bilateral cooperation.
8 Nov — Tripoli: Egypt reopened its embassy after a 12-year closure on security grounds.

8 Nov — Tripoli: PM Dbeibah met UN envoy Hanna Tetteh to review the UN-sponsored 4+4 committee's work on the electoral commission and election timetable; no armed clashes were found in reporting for 5–12 Nov.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. No armed clashes, drone attacks or oil blockades were reported this week. Diplomatic activity is increasing: UNSMIL's renewal, the 4+4 election track, Egypt's return to Tripoli, and the Haftar family's outreach to Niger. This modestly stabilises the political track but does not resolve the east–west split. The structural risk is unchanged: Zawiya and Surman have seen more than 30 armed clashes in 2026, the Zawiya refinery and power grid were hit by drones in August, and the Haftar succession is still open. Over the next 90 days, watch for renewed militia fighting west of Tripoli, disputes over the central bank and maritime deals, and any slippage in the election timetable. Sustained fighting would justify HIGH.

forecasts.statement: Armed clashes between rival groups in Zawiya or Surman kill three or more people in a single episode.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, Libya Observer, Libya Security Monitor or UNSMIL report at least three deaths from one episode of armed clashes in Zawiya or Surman between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

countries.name: Tunisia
incidents: 23 Oct — Tunis / Jebiniana (Sfax governorate): Rare unrest broke out over recent deaths linked to the police; protesters burned a vehicle and tyres, and police fired tear gas.
17 Oct — Tunis: Thousands joined the largest protest against President Saied in years, over economic hardship and restrictions on political freedoms, with hundreds of police deployed.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. No new incidents were found this week, but the underlying tension has not eased. Tunisia saw its largest anti-Saied protest in years in October, followed by clashes over deaths linked to the police. The Court of Cassation confirmed the mass 'conspiracy' sentences, and the state of emergency remains in force until 31 December. There is no organised armed violence, so HIGH does not apply, and the protest wave is too recent to justify LOW. Over the next 90 days, expect further economically driven protests and anger at the police, more prosecutions of opposition figures and activists, and a risk of deadly escalation if security forces use more force. Smuggling along the Libyan border is a secondary risk.

regions.name: Ukraine/Russia
overview: The first trilateral round in Abu Dhabi (10–11 November) produced a humanitarian result but no political breakthrough. Russia and Ukraine agreed a large-scale prisoner exchange, which TASS says should take place within two to three weeks, with numbers to be fixed on 12 November. No ceasefire, territorial or security-guarantee deal was announced. Kushner called it 'very tough but productive', citing progress on a post-war security framework and saying territory remains the hardest issue. Witkoff and Kushner arrived in Moscow on 12 November to brief Putin and are due to meet Zelensky in Dublin afterwards. Kyiv wants future rounds to include Europe, and Medinsky says Moscow does not object to EU participation.

Russia's winter strike campaign continues without pause. The Komyshuvakha (Zaporizhzhia) glide-bomb strike of 2 November is now the deadliest Russian strike of 2026: the toll passed 50 by 6 November, and CNN cites local authorities confirming 53. A drone again targeted rescuers at the site on 8 November. Ukraine's Energy Ministry counted 128 attacks on the energy sector in one week, and the overnight attack of 10–11 November (163 drones plus Kh-59/69 and Banderol/Dan-T cruise missiles) caused outages in eight oblasts, with 9 killed nationwide in a day.

Ukraine's deep-strike campaign has reached the Baltic coast again. On 9 November drones set Russia's second-largest refinery at Kirishi (Leningrad Oblast) on fire, and the General Staff says it hit the Morozov plant, which makes Iskander propellant and explosives. Border regions keep taking casualties, with one person killed in Kursk Oblast on 8 November and one in Graivoron (Belgorod) on 11–12 November. On the ground, ISW assesses Russia lost net territory in October for the second month running. Kostiantynivka is still contested after a year of urban fighting, with Russian forces in roughly a third of the town, while DeepState reports small Russian gains on the Siversk axis.

The periphery stays below the threshold of hostilities, but spillover continues. Two Russian Banderol cruise missiles crossed Moldovan airspace from Odesa Oblast on 11 November, the latest in a string of autumn incursions. Georgia's party-ban case was delayed by a judge's illness and resumes on 12 November, with the question stage expected to run to 17 November, while the 68th Geneva International Discussions round was scheduled for 10–11 November. In Armenia, opposition leader Samvel Karapetyan was detained for a month and an opposition detainee died in custody on 10 November, which sharpens the constitutional-referendum fight. Azerbaijan marked Victory Day on 8 November without reported incidents, and the Karimli trial on the merits starts 13 November.

countries.name: Ukraine
incidents: 6 Nov — Komyshuvakha (Zaporizhzhia Oblast): The death toll from the 2 November guided-bomb strike on an aid-distribution school and shelter rose to at least 50 after more bodies were recovered, and CNN cites local authorities confirming 53, making it Russia's deadliest strike of 2026. On 8 November a drone again targeted emergency workers at the site, per the State Emergency Service.

9 Nov — Odesa: A Russian attack killed three people and seriously wounded one, per the city military administration. Russia also struck three power substations and a cargo ship in the Black Sea that Moscow claimed was carrying arms; Ukraine's Energy Ministry counted 128 attacks on the energy sector in the past week.

10–11 Nov — Nationwide: An overnight attack with 163 drones (91 jet-powered), a Kh-59/69 and Banderol/Dan-T cruise missiles killed 9 and injured 39 over the day, including 3 dead in Dnipropetrovsk, 2 in Donetsk, 2 in Odesa, 1 in Kherson and 1 in Zaporizhzhia oblasts. Power outages were reported in eight oblasts including Kyiv, Kharkiv and Odesa.

10–11 Nov — Abu Dhabi (UAE): US-mediated trilateral talks with Russia ended with agreement on a large-scale prisoner exchange, expected within two to three weeks, but no ceasefire or territorial agreement. Arakhamia cited 'good momentum' and called for Europe to join future rounds.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Ukraine remains under full-scale attack. In the past week the Komyshuvakha toll passed 50, Odesa and the east took repeated lethal strikes, and the energy grid was hit 128 times in seven days. Over the next 90 days, expect Russia to keep up mixed salvos of jet drones, Banderol and Kh-59/69 cruise missiles and ballistic missiles against power, heating and rail, with heavy glide bombs on front-line towns in Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts and rolling outages across Kyiv, Kharkiv, Sumy and Odesa. On the ground, Russian pressure is grinding rather than decisive. ISW assesses net Russian territorial losses in October, the tempo around Sloviansk–Kramatorsk is stalling on manpower, and Ukrainian forces have advanced near Orikhiv. Kostiantynivka is the most likely urban loss, but Russian forces hold only about a third of it after a year of fighting, so full capture before mid-February is unlikely. The Siversk axis is the most active local Russian push. On diplomacy, the agreed prisoner exchange is the most probable concrete result and is likely to happen within weeks. The Witkoff–Kushner Moscow visit and a possible wider format with Europe are the variables to watch. A general or energy ceasefire within 90 days remains unlikely because Moscow still ties it to territorial concessions. Watch for the size and timing of the exchange, whether talks resume with European participation, Russian progress inside Kostiantynivka, and generating capacity lost after each mass strike.

forecasts.statement: Russian forces take full control of the town of Kostiantynivka (Donetsk Oblast).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if DeepState's map or ISW's assessment shows the whole built-up area of Kostiantynivka under Russian control (a Russian MoD claim alone does not count).

countries.name: Russia
incidents: 9 Nov — Kirishi (Leningrad Oblast): Ukrainian drones set the KINEF refinery, Russia's second-largest, on fire, hitting at least one crude-processing unit. Governor Drozdenko said 113 drones were downed; Al Jazeera reported him saying a woman was killed by debris, while Kyiv Post reported no injuries in Kirishi. Ukraine's General Staff also claimed a strike on the Rostec-owned Morozov plant, which makes explosives and Iskander propellant.
8 Nov — Kursk Oblast: One person was killed when a Ukrainian drone hit a tractor, per Governor Khinshtein (Reuters).

11–12 Nov — Graivoron district (Belgorod Oblast): One civilian was killed and eight injured over the past day, per the regional governor. Russia's Defence Ministry claimed 71 Ukrainian drones downed overnight into 12 November over seven regions and Crimea.

12 Nov — Moscow: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner arrived to brief Putin on the Abu Dhabi talks, which ended on 11 November with a prisoner-exchange agreement but no ceasefire; Medinsky said Moscow is not opposed to EU participation in future talks.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Russia is waging an active war and its own territory is under sustained attack. Ukrainian drones reached the Baltic coast refinery at Kirishi and an Iskander propellant plant near St Petersburg this week, and border regions such as Kursk and Belgorod see deaths nearly every week. Over the next 90 days, expect the Kremlin to bank the Abu Dhabi humanitarian track and the Witkoff–Kushner channel to push for a broad US–Russia arrangement, including sanctions relief and recognition of territorial gains, while rejecting a general ceasefire. The agreed prisoner exchange is likely to happen in the coming weeks as a low-cost goodwill signal. Expect the winter strike campaign against Ukraine's grid to continue at full intensity and deniable pressure on Black Sea shipping to persist. Ukraine will keep hitting refineries, ports and defence plants, causing local fuel disruption and recurring airport closures around Moscow and St Petersburg. Drone alerts near the Baltic states keep a NATO airspace incident possible. The regime's internal grip remains firm, and political stability risk is low. Watch for the size and timing of the prisoner exchange, Putin's response to the envoys, and whether Ukraine's strikes widen to Baltic export terminals.

forecasts.statement: Russia and Ukraine carry out a prisoner exchange in which each side releases at least 500 prisoners of war (in one swap or in stages announced as part of the Abu Dhabi deal).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP or the Kyiv Independent reports that at least 500 POWs per side have been exchanged under the agreement by that date, per official Ukrainian or Russian statements.

countries.name: Belarus
incidents: 3 Nov — Minsk: At the Minsk International Conference on Eurasian Security, Lukashenka warned that cost-of-living protests across Europe could spread to and destabilise Belarus, and repeated his offer to host peace talks.

31 Oct — Gomel: Four evacuation flights carrying hundreds of residents from occupied Oleshky (Kherson Oblast) landed in Gomel, from where evacuees continued to Ukrainian-controlled territory, making Belarus a transit point for the US-brokered humanitarian arrangement.

11 Nov — Minsk: In a message for Poland's Independence Day, Lukashenka said Minsk is ready to resume dialogue with Warsaw and urged both sides to drop confrontation (per UA.News; not yet confirmed by other outlets).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. This was a quiet week. No hostilities on Belarusian territory, armed border incidents or troop build-ups toward Ukraine or NATO were reported. Belarus's profile remains indirect support for Russia's war plus militarisation and coercive signalling, now softened by outreach to Warsaw and a self-presented role as humanitarian and diplomatic facilitator. Over the next 90 days, expect Minsk to use the momentum from Abu Dhabi to revive its prisoner-for-sanctions bargaining with Washington. Envoy Coale's return visit is overdue and could bring another release. Expect smuggling-balloon friction with Lithuania and Poland during the winter wind season, continued territorial-defence drills and domestic repression. A rise to HIGH would require direct military coercion of a NATO neighbour, a serious armed border incident, or Belarusian forces joining the war.

countries.name: Moldova
incidents: 11 Nov — Southern border (from Odesa Oblast): Two Russian Banderol (S8000) cruise missiles entered Moldovan airspace at 06:04 and 06:06 during an overnight attack on Ukraine and left after four to five minutes, per the Defence Ministry. No impacts or casualties were reported.

31 Oct — Rîbnița/Călărași and Dondușeni/Edineț districts: Two Russian drones violated Moldovan airspace during mass attacks on Ukraine, one routed over the Transnistrian region; the Defence Ministry temporarily closed airspace over the north and centre. No crashes or casualties were reported.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Airspace violations have escalated from drones to cruise missiles: two Banderol missiles crossed on 11 November, following drone incursions on 31 October and a 23 October crash near homes. There are still no casualties and no evidence of deliberate targeting, so the HIGH threshold is not met. Over the next 90 days, expect more crossings whenever Russia attacks Odesa and Vinnytsia oblasts, more temporary airspace closures, and a realistic possibility of another crash or debris impact on Moldovan soil. Expect diplomatic protests, faster EU-funded air surveillance and counter-drone purchases, and continued Russian hybrid pressure through cyber activity, Gagauzia and Transnistria's winter energy squeeze. A first fatality, damage to critical infrastructure, or evidence of deliberate targeting would justify a review toward HIGH.

forecasts.statement: A Russian drone or missile, or identifiable wreckage of one, falls on Moldovan territory (crash or impact, not only an overflight).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Moldova's Defence Ministry or police report a crash, impact or recovered wreckage of a Russian drone or missile on Moldovan territory, as reported by Reuters, AP or Moldovan official channels.

countries.name: Georgia
incidents: 9 Nov — Tbilisi: The Constitutional Court postponed the scheduled resumption of the Georgian Dream petition to ban five opposition parties because a judge fell ill. Hearings resume on 12 November with judges questioning party representatives, a stage expected to run to 17 November.

10–11 Nov — Geneva: The 68th round of the Geneva International Discussions on the Abkhazia and South Ossetia conflicts was scheduled, with Russia again pressing for a non-use-of-force agreement; no outcome had been reported at the time of writing.
4 Nov — Tbilisi: UNM politician Giorgi Baramidze was remanded in custody on a treason (sabotage) charge over remarks about the 1992–93 Abkhazia conflict.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. There is no organised political violence. Repression runs through the courts: the party-ban case, a treason charge against an opposition politician over his statements, and protest-related detentions under the new laws on road blocking and face masks. Daily Rustaveli protests continue, and police occasionally use tear gas and water cannon, but casualties remain limited. Over the next 90 days, the party-ban case is the key variable. The court has rejected every opposition motion and the question stage ends around 17 November, so a ruling banning at least one party before mid-February is a realistic possibility, perhaps timed around the 28 November opposition rally. Expect more criminal cases against opposition figures, deeper conflict with the EU, and routine detentions along the South Ossetia line. Banning the main opposition parties combined with mass protests that are violently dispersed would justify HIGH.

forecasts.statement: Georgia's Constitutional Court rules to ban (declare unconstitutional) at least one of the five opposition parties named in the Georgian Dream petition.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Civil.ge, Georgia Today, JAMnews or Reuters reports a Constitutional Court ruling banning at least one of UNM, Coalition for Change, Strong Georgia/Lelo, the Federalists or Gakharia for Georgia by that date.

countries.name: Armenia
incidents: 4–5 Nov — Yerevan: Investigators detained Strong Armenia leader Samvel Karapetyan over alleged abuses said to have cost the national power distributor $179mn, and the Anti-Corruption Court ordered him held for one month. His party calls it persecution linked to the constitutional-referendum fight.

10 Nov — Yerevan (Nubarashen prison): Opposition-aligned detainee Arsen Gevorgyan died in custody less than three weeks after his arrest; Justice Minister Galyan cited cardiac arrest without giving the underlying cause.
11 Nov — Yerevan: Strong Armenia protested outside the EU Delegation over what it calls political persecution and EU silence; Moscow has condemned Yerevan's pressure on the opposition.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. There are no hostilities and no fatal border incidents. Political tension has sharpened: the main opposition leader has been jailed, a detainee died in custody, and this follows the 29 October parliamentary brawl. This is still repression and polarisation with limited violence, not organised political violence. Over the next 90 days, expect the government to push the draft constitution toward a referendum, which Baku makes a precondition for the peace treaty. Civil Contract's 64 seats fall short of the 70 needed, which raises the incentive to pressure opposition MPs, so expect more detentions and court extensions such as Tsarukyan's. Protests by Strong Armenia and church-aligned groups are likely to grow, and Moscow will keep amplifying them diplomatically. TRIPP design work and the gradual handover of border control from Russian forces will continue. Violent street unrest, a deliberate shooting, or armed border incidents would warrant a review toward HIGH.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
incidents: 8 Nov — Baku: Azerbaijan marked Victory Day, the sixth anniversary of the 2020 war, with official ceremonies and a concert on Baku Boulevard; no security incidents were reported.

2–3 Nov — Goytepe (Iranian border): Border guards shot dead an armed man who opened fire while crossing illegally from Iran; a criminal case was opened and Tehran was notified. Drones that entered Azerbaijani airspace were neutralised and drug-smuggling attempts in the Horadiz and Goytepe areas were stopped.

4 Nov — Baku: Azerbaijan declared 14 Iranian citizens persona non grata over statements it called hostile. The closed preliminary hearing against Popular Front chairman Ali Karimli, charged with attempting to seize power, began, with the trial on the merits set for 13 November.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. This was a quiet week with little new reporting. There are no hostilities on Azerbaijani territory. Friction with Iran, including the armed smuggler incident, drone incursions and the expulsion of 14 Iranians, has not turned into military escalation, and Victory Day passed without incident. Domestic pressure takes the form of prosecutions: the Karimli coup case and the Meydan TV and Toplum TV cases. Over the next 90 days, expect the Karimli trial from 13 November to bring tight security and international criticism. Expect continued in-absentia charges against critics abroad, recurring smuggling and drone incidents on the Iranian border, and a slow peace track with Armenia that hinges on Yerevan's constitutional referendum, where Armenia's domestic crackdown adds uncertainty. Violent clashes during protests, or a pattern of armed incidents on the Armenian or Iranian border, would warrant a review toward HIGH.

regions.name: Sahel
overview: Sudan's war widened again in Blue Nile and Kordofan. The RSF–SPLM-N 'Tasis' alliance released footage from Maqja (Bau locality, about 90 km from Ed Damazin) on 6 November, after taking Sali, Al-Keili and Bakori. An RSF drone strike on Bani Shako village (Kurmuk) killed nine civilians on 10 November. In Kordofan, the army and the Joint Force launched simultaneous attacks in North and West Kordofan on 5–6 November, and both sides made competing, unverified claims of success.

The Sudan war is taking on a regional dimension. On 4 November Ethiopia expelled six Sudanese consular staff from Assosa and closed the consulate there, and Khartoum retaliated by closing Ethiopia's consulate in Gedaref. The move followed Sudanese accusations that drones were being launched against it from Ethiopian territory. Combined with the RSF's late-October drone campaign against the power grid, this points to a long war of attrition on infrastructure, with a growing cross-border risk.

In Nigeria, killings continued in the north-west and the middle belt. Bandits killed a vigilante and ten members of his family in Maradun (Zamfara) on 7 November, and attacks in Plateau and Benue killed at least 11 people over 3–8 November. In the north-east, the military reported heavy ISWAP losses from air strikes near Wulgo (Ngala) on 10 November and in Borno/Yobe operations; these figures are not independently verified.

In the central Sahel, independent reporting remains very thin because of junta information controls. Mali's army reported air strikes near Ménaka (6 Nov) and south of Kidal (7 Nov), and JNIM claimed an IED strike on a FAMa/Africa Corps vehicle on the Sévaré–Konna road (2 Nov). AFP analysis (6 Nov) describes Burkina Faso's war as less deadly since late June but with an unrelenting attack tempo. No verified attack was found in Niger. In Chad, a 30 October farmer–herder clash at Koula killed 25, and the Tibesti fighting with the Miski militia remains unresolved and unreported.

countries.name: Mali
incidents: 2 Nov — Sévaré–Konna road, Mopti region: JNIM claimed an IED strike on a vehicle carrying Malian soldiers and Russian Africa Corps personnel. Casualties and location rest only on the group's claim; Bamako released no toll.
6 Nov — About 50 km south-west of Ménaka: The army general staff said it struck a group of armed fighters with war materiel after confirming the target. It gave no casualty figures.
7 Nov — About 90 km south of Kidal: The army said it struck six positions held by armed groups and that reconnaissance was continuing to assess the results. No toll was given.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. JNIM, the FLA and IS Sahel still hold or contest large areas. The army's continued air strikes in the Ménaka and Kidal regions and JNIM's IED campaign on the Mopti axis show that hostilities are ongoing, so a week with little verified reporting does not justify a lower level. Over the next 90 days FAMa and the Africa Corps will likely keep using air and drone strikes in the north and centre while trying to hold Kidal and the routes north. JNIM is likely to keep up IED and ambush attacks around Sévaré, Konna and Douentza, and to keep pressure on the fuel corridors into Bamako. Escorted tanker convoys from Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire are likely targets as dry-season mobility improves, and a convoy attack with ten or more deaths is a realistic possibility. IS Sahel violence around Ménaka is likely to continue. The AES summit diplomacy (Goïta in Niamey on 5 Nov) is unlikely to change the battlefield in the short term. Watch for a large garrison assault, a tightened blockade around Bamako, or signs of strain inside the junta.

forecasts.statement: JNIM attacks a fuel tanker convoy anywhere in Mali in an incident that reportedly kills ten or more people (drivers, escorts or civilians).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, RFI or ACLED reports a single JNIM attack on a fuel convoy in Mali on or before 31 Jan 2027 with a reported toll of at least ten dead.

countries.name: Niger
incidents: 5 Nov — Niamey: Mali's leader Assimi Goïta visited Niamey, where he and Gen. Tiani praised the unified AES force's results against terrorism, according to Nigerien media.

c. 10–12 Nov — Niamey: The junta again protested against what it called the EU's 'repeated interference' in its internal affairs. Following protests from Niamey and Algiers, an EU spokesperson issued a clarification.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained: the threat has not decreased. ISSP killed more than 50 soldiers and gendarmes in two attacks near Abala-Filingué and Birni-N'Konni in late September, and the junta survived a coup attempt on 28–29 August. A second week without verified reporting does not indicate calm. Over the next 90 days ISSP ambushes on convoys and posts in Tillabéri and the Tahoua–Dosso belt are likely to continue, JNIM is likely to keep pressing in the south-west toward Benin, and Boko Haram/ISWAP attacks around Diffa remain likely. The unresolved Emiloulou drone-strike dispute with Chad and the friction with the EU feed the junta's sovereignty narrative and keep the risk of proxy activity along the Chad border. Another coup attempt or mutiny remains a realistic risk while the army purge continues.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
incidents: 6 Nov — Nationwide: AFP analysis reported that large-scale jihadist attacks have stopped since late June, but that attacks remain frequent and less deadly. Analysts attribute the lull to operational factors rather than any loss of jihadist capability.
Late Oct — Burkina Faso: The state news agency AIB reported that the army killed a JNIM commander accused of several attacks on the army and VDP militias.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. JNIM and IS Sahel still fight the state and each other across much of the country. HRW's 4 November report documented JNIM massacres in Yatenga in September, and ACLED counted 125 JNIM attacks on civilians from January to August. The AFP-reported drop in large attacks since late June is not a sign the conflict has receded: attack frequency remains high and analysts say JNIM's capacity has grown through ransoms and prisoner exchanges. Over the next 90 days the dry season is likely to bring renewed large garrison assaults in the North, Sahel, East and Boucle du Mouhoun regions, and continued sieges of towns such as Djibo. The JNIM–IS Sahel contest in Oudalan is likely to keep producing clashes. Repression of dissent and suspected collaborators will likely continue. Analysts should rely on group claims, displacement data and rights-group reporting given the blackout.

countries.name: Sudan
incidents: 10 Nov — Bani Shako, Kurmuk county, Blue Nile: An RSF drone strike killed nine civilians and seriously injured several others, according to the Kurmuk commissioner. The RSF did not comment.

6 Nov — Maqja, Bau locality, Blue Nile: The RSF–SPLM-N 'Tasis' alliance released videos of its fighters inside Maqja, about 90 km from Ed Damazin. The army neither confirmed nor denied the loss; the regional government acknowledged changes in territorial control.

5–6 Nov — North/West Kordofan: The army and the Joint Force launched simultaneous attacks on RSF positions. The Joint Force claimed to have retaken Umm Sumayma, Kazgeil, Al-Hammadi and Abu Quoud and destroyed 40 vehicles, while pro-RSF media claimed an ambush and an army retreat to El Obeid. Neither claim was verified.

4 Nov — Assosa/Gedaref: Ethiopia expelled six Sudanese consular staff and closed Sudan's consulate in Assosa, and Sudan closed Ethiopia's consulate in Gedaref in response. Khartoum accuses Ethiopia of allowing drone attacks from its territory, which Addis Ababa denies.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained: full-scale war continues on several fronts. In Blue Nile the RSF–SPLM-N alliance keeps gaining ground (Sali, Al-Keili, Bakori, now Maqja) and is striking civilians with drones. In Kordofan the army has launched a new offensive on the North/West Kordofan border while both sides trade drone attacks. Over the next 90 days the alliance is likely to press toward Ed Damazin and the Roseires axis, while the army tries to retake lost bases; a full army recapture of Sali is unlikely in that time. The Ethiopia–Sudan diplomatic rupture raises the risk of the Blue Nile front becoming a cross-border theatre. In Kordofan, fighting around El Obeid, Babanusa and the oil areas of West Kordofan is likely to intensify in the dry season, with more air and drone strikes on populated areas. The RSF's drone campaign against power, water and fuel infrastructure is likely to continue, deepening shortages and famine conditions and stranding aid. With continuing foreign arms flows and no credible talks, a truce is unlikely. Expect continued displacement into Chad, South Sudan and Ethiopia.

events.place: Bani Shako, Kurmuk county, Blue Nile

forecasts.statement: The Sudanese Armed Forces and allied forces retake the Sali military base in Blue Nile from the RSF–SPLM-N alliance.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Sudan Tribune, Dabanga, Sudans Post, Reuters or AP reports, on or before 12 Feb 2027, that SAF or allied forces have regained control of Sali (an SAF claim corroborated by footage or a second independent source counts).

countries.name: Chad
incidents: 30 Oct — Koula (Hadjer-Lamis/Bahr El-Ghazal border): A dispute over access to a pond between a Kreda herder and a Kouka farmer escalated into armed intercommunal clashes. The territorial administration ministry confirmed 25 dead and 22 wounded, and 39 people were arrested and transferred to N'Djamena.
11 Nov — Abéché, Ouaddaï: President Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno held the fourth stage of a security tour of the east, focusing on local security and relations between communities.
5–12 Nov — Tibesti: No new official information on the army's fighting with the Miski Self-Defence Committee, which began on 14 Oct. The lack of news is not evidence that the clashes have ended.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Chad faces repeated lethal intercommunal violence (Koula, 25 dead on 30 Oct; Mouray, 12 dead on 18–19 Oct), an unresolved armed standoff with the Miski militia in Tibesti, spillover from the Sudan war on its eastern border, and Boko Haram activity around Lake Chad. It is not raised to CRITICAL because the state still controls the wider territory and the Tibesti fighting remains confined to one mining area. Over the next 90 days dry-season transhumance is likely to bring further deadly farmer–herder clashes in the centre and east, which the president's security tour is meant to contain. A forcible army push to retake Miski is possible but the government seems to prefer containment, so a full recapture is unlikely in this period; heavy confirmed losses there, or repeated large cross-border strikes from Sudan, would justify CRITICAL. The Emiloulou dispute with Niger is likely to stay a source of rhetorical escalation. Refugee arrivals from Darfur will stay high.

forecasts.statement: The Chadian army takes control of the town of Miski in Tibesti from the Miski Self-Defence Committee, by force or under a negotiated handover.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if AFP, Reuters, RFI or Crisis Group reports on or before 12 Feb 2027 that Chadian state forces control Miski town.

countries.name: Mauritania
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. There is no organised armed violence inside the country; the risks come from border friction with Mali, the pressure of around 300,000 Malian refugees in Hodh Chargui, migration flows and limited social unrest. Elite army units hold military zones along the Mali border. Over the next 90 days, FAMa and Africa Corps strikes near Ménaka, Timbuktu and Ségou, together with JNIM activity in western Mali, are likely to push more refugees into Hodh Chargui and risk incidents involving Mauritanian herders, keeping relations with Bamako tense. Nouakchott will likely continue containment through diplomatic protests and precautionary measures. A JNIM attack inside Mauritania or an armed border clash would justify HIGH; neither is likely in this period.

countries.name: Nigeria
incidents: 7 Nov — Gidan Taba, Maradun LGA, Zamfara: Gunmen killed a vigilante and ten members of his family and set their house on fire, according to police, who also reported 13 residents abducted. Some reports put the toll at 12.
8 Nov — Bel village, Barkin Ladi LGA, Plateau: Gunmen killed three civilians and a soldier, part of attacks in Plateau and Benue that killed at least 11 people over 3–8 Nov.

10 Nov — Near Wulgo–Momaduru, Ngala LGA, Borno: Operation Hadin Kai air strikes hit a large gathering of suspected fighters; the military said 40 ISWAP fighters were killed. The toll is not independently verified.

c. 10–11 Nov — Bulabulutube (Borno) and Gujba (Yobe): The military said air strikes and a joint ground ambush killed at least 20 suspected terrorists, including ISWAP fighters. The claim is not independently verified.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Insurgency in the north-east, bandit massacres in the north-west and repeated killings in Plateau and Benue continue every week, with attacks on both civilians and security forces (including the 3 Nov ambush on police guarding a Senate primary in Zamfara). Over the next 90 days ISWAP is likely to keep up night raids on forward bases in Kukawa, Ngala, Marte, Guzamala and the Lake Chad islands as dry-season mobility improves, along with IED and ambush attacks on supply routes; a single attack on a military base killing ten or more soldiers is likely. The military will continue to claim high enemy tolls from air and amphibious operations that are hard to verify, with a standing risk of civilian casualties. Bandit groups in Zamfara, Katsina and Sokoto are likely to keep carrying out mass killings and kidnappings and to target security forces and party events as the election cycle advances. Farmer–herder and reprisal violence in Plateau and Benue is likely to continue.

events.place: Bel village, Barkin Ladi LGA, Plateau

forecasts.statement: ISWAP or Boko Haram fighters attack a military base or forward position in Borno or Yobe in a single attack that reportedly kills ten or more Nigerian soldiers.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, HumAngle, Premium Times or Daily Trust reports, on or before 12 Feb 2027, a single attack in Borno or Yobe in which at least ten soldiers were killed (military, security-source or credible local tolls count).

regions.name: Asia-Pacific
overview: China is running its largest maritime show of force of 2026 without naming it. Taiwan's NSC counted more than 100 PLAN and China Coast Guard ships off Taiwan, in the South China Sea and in the Western Pacific as of 3 November. AEI/ISW link task groups from three theatre commands, including the Liaoning carrier group, to a possible rehearsal of isolating Taiwan, and on 10 November Taiwan's defence minister called it 'area denial' drills. Around Taiwan the MND recorded 111 PLA sorties in the week of 2–8 November. On 9 November four CCG ships entered Senkaku territorial waters for the first time since 10 October. The APEC summit in Shenzhen next week and Taiwan's 28 November local elections are the near-term triggers.

Pakistan's internal war produced the region's deadliest single attack of the week. On 11 November militants ambushed a police team near Kohat (KP), killing 10 officers including a DSP; police say 18 attackers died, and the TTP claimed responsibility. An IED killed a bomb-disposal officer in South Waziristan on 7 November. Around 5 November Pakistani troops and Afghan Taliban forces exchanged heavy fire in Kurram's Shalozan sector. KP is now under Governor's Rule, and no ceasefire with Kabul is in place.

Myanmar's regime kept up an air campaign that kills civilians and is pushing on several fronts. On 7 November gyrocopter bombs on a school and homes in Kani Township (Sagaing) killed 11, including teachers and children. A 6 November strike in KNU-held Tanintharyi killed three civilians. Ground operations displaced more than 15,000 people in Kyaikto (Mon), and on 11 November the junta claimed to have taken eleven resistance positions since early November. Shells from fighting at Myawaddy damaged houses in Thailand's Mae Sot on 7 November.

The Korean peninsula moved from launches to rhetoric. After the 4 November Sondok missile launch and a new air-defence missile test, no further launch was found for 5–12 November. On 10 November Kim Yo Jong rejected the UN Secretary-General's call for inter-Korean dialogue and denied responsibility for the September DMZ mine blast. The loudspeaker threat and MDL friction remain unresolved. Elsewhere violence stayed local: in India, killings continued in Manipur on 12 November and two SPOs were found shot dead in Kishtwar (J&K). In Bangladesh, garment-wage unrest continued in Gazipur, and in Thailand security forces killed a wanted insurgent in Yala on 9 November.

countries.name: North Korea
incidents: 2 Nov — Undisclosed site (KCNA, 3 Nov): North Korea tested a dispersal (cluster) warhead for a strategic cruise missile, the second new cluster-type warhead trial in a week.

4 Nov — Sondok, South Hamgyong: Multiple missiles were fired toward the East Sea, which Reuters called the fourth weapons launch in a month. The same day KCNA said a newly designed advanced air-defence missile system was test-fired, guided by CMC member Gen. Kim Jong Sik, alongside a strategic cruise-missile strike drill.

3–4 Nov — Pyongyang: Kim Yo Jong called US allegations that North Korea stole more than $6 billion from Binance 'absurd' and warned of a stronger response to US 'hostile policy'. On 6 Nov the US cut off the exchanger MEXC over transactions involving North Korea.

10 Nov — Pyongyang: Kim Yo Jong rejected UN Secretary-General Guterres' call for inter-Korean dialogue, accused him of speaking for Seoul, and again denied responsibility for the September DMZ mine blast.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Four weapons events in the month to 4 November (an SRBM salvo, two cluster-warhead trials and a new air-defence missile) were followed by a quieter week of hostile rhetoric aimed at Washington, Seoul and the UN. Over the next 90 days, expect further short-range ballistic and cruise-missile launches, some timed to allied drills or to US–China summitry such as the APEC meeting in Shenzhen. Expect year-end announcements tied to the pledge to deploy new warhead types to units, and continued cyber theft to fund the programme. Pyongyang is likely to keep refusing Seoul's MDL talks offer and to deny responsibility for the September mine blast. Fortification work along the MDL will keep drawing South Korean warning fire, although winter may slow it. The main escalation paths are an exchange of fire at the DMZ or a salvo toward the NLL. An ICBM or nuclear test remains a low-probability wildcard.

forecasts.statement: North Korea launches at least one ballistic missile that South Korea's JCS publicly reports.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the JCS (as reported by Yonhap, Reuters or AP) announces at least one North Korean ballistic missile launch between 2026-11-12 and 2026-12-31. Cruise-missile or artillery-only launches do not count.

countries.name: Myanmar
incidents: 7 Nov — Nyaung Pin Le village, Kani Township, Sagaing: Three regime gyrocopters dropped bombs on a school and homes at about 11:30, killing 11 people, including teachers and children, and injuring about 10, according to m.CDM and Myanmar Now.

6 Nov — Mazaw village, Ler Mu Lah Township (KNU Myeik-Dawei District): The KNU said an airstrike by a fighter jet and three gyrocopters killed three civilians, including a child, and injured seven, damaging a preschool building.

3–6 Nov — Kyaikto Township, Mon State, and Salingyi Township, Sagaing: Junta ground operations forced resistance forces to withdraw from a base near Khamauk Khwe and displaced more than 15,000 residents. On 6 Nov troops burned hundreds of houses in Kyaing Khamauk village, Salingyi.

11 Nov — Nationwide: The junta said its forces had taken eleven positions from the NUG, KNU and PDFs since early November, including an NUG 'Special Military Region'. The claim has not been independently verified.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Mass-casualty air attacks on schools, clinics and villages continued in Sagaing and Tanintharyi after the 1 November Rakhine strikes, and junta ground offensives in Mon, Sagaing and Karen states displaced tens of thousands. The NUG counted 641 aerial bombing attacks killing 212 civilians in October alone. Over the next 90 days, expect the regime to keep pairing gyrocopter and jet strikes with clearance operations along the Mandalay–Sagaing corridor and in the southeast, and to keep bombarding AA-held Rakhine townships. The AA will keep tightening its grip on Sittwe, which has already cost the navy several ships, but a full capture within the window is not the most likely outcome given the junta's fortifications and naval resupply. Cross-border spillover into Thailand around Myawaddy will recur. No negotiated de-escalation is in sight.

Mazaw village, Ler Mu Lah Township

forecasts.statement: The Arakan Army takes full control of Sittwe, the Rakhine State capital, with junta forces withdrawn or defeated.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, The Irrawaddy or DVB report by 2027-02-12 that the AA controls Sittwe town and the regime's regional command there has fallen or withdrawn. AA claims alone do not count.

countries.name: Pakistan
incidents: 11 Nov — Darbukach, Gumbat area near Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Militants ambushed a police team returning from an operation against illegal gold mining, killing 10 police including DSP Haidar Zaman and wounding 12. Police said 18 attackers were killed, and the TTP claimed responsibility as part of a series of attacks.
7 Nov — Janta, Sararogha tehsil, Upper South Waziristan: An IED killed Abdul Jabbar, an assistant head of the police Bomb Disposal Squad, as he tried to defuse it.

5 Nov — Shalozan sector, Kurram: Pakistani troops exchanged heavy-weapons fire with Afghan Taliban forces after stopping an attempted cross-border infiltration by suspected TTP militants. Casualties were not established and ISPR did not comment.
Early Nov — Mohmand district, KP: Unidentified gunmen killed two policemen and wounded one, Dawn reported.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The Kohat ambush, the deadliest attack on police in KP in weeks, came under Governor's Rule and shows the TTP can still mount company-size operations. Border clashes with the Afghan Taliban (Torkham, South Waziristan, Kurram) continue without a ceasefire. Over the next 90 days, expect frequent TTP attacks on police and FC posts in Kohat, Bannu, Lakki Marwat, Dera Ismail Khan and the former tribal districts, and recurrent IEDs and quadcopter attacks. Large ISPR 'intelligence-based operations' will follow. The BLA's ambush and highway-blockade campaign in Kharan, Kech, Mastung and Nushki will continue, with claims and official figures diverging. After a mass-casualty TTP attack, Pakistani airstrikes on TTP targets inside Afghanistan are likely, which would set off another round of cross-border fighting.
