Janta, Sararogha tehsil, Upper South Waziristan

forecasts.statement: Pakistan carries out at least one airstrike or drone strike inside Afghan territory.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP or Al Jazeera report by 2027-02-12 a Pakistani air or drone strike on Afghan territory, confirmed by Pakistan or reported by the Taliban government. Cross-border artillery or small-arms fire alone does not count.

countries.name: India
incidents: 12 Nov — Taphou village, Senapati district, Manipur: Gunmen fired on villagers working in paddy fields along NH-2, killing a woman and wounding two men. Organiser blames suspected Kuki militants, which is unverified. The CM had visited Taphou on 9 Nov to defuse tensions after two local youths were found dead on 1 Nov.
12 Nov — Sinakeithel village, Ukhrul district, Manipur: Suspected armed miscreants fired from the Lungter Hills at farmers harvesting paddy and wounded one. Security forces returned fire.
11 Nov — Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir: Unidentified gunmen opened fire on a CRPF patrol, injuring three personnel, one critically. A search for two militants resumed.
11–12 Nov — Kishtwar, Jammu and Kashmir: The bodies of two missing Special Police Officers were found with bullet wounds and their service weapons missing, and police suspect militants.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Kuki–Naga violence in Manipur produced new fatal shootings on 12 November, after at least eight conflict deaths between 31 October and 4 November. In Jammu and Kashmir, the CRPF patrol attack in Kulgam and the killing of two SPOs in Kishtwar show that militant cells in the south and in the Chenab valley remain active. Over the next 90 days, expect tit-for-tat shootings, abductions and highway blockades along NH-2 (Kangpokpi–Senapati), in Noney and in Ukhrul, intra-Naga factional clashes, and Meitei protests over the Kuki ceasefire arrangement. In J&K, expect hit-and-run attacks on security forces and search operations in Kishtwar, Doda and Kulgam, while infiltration attempts drop as snow closes the passes. India–Pakistan friction remains rhetorical with no LoC incident found.

countries.name: China
incidents: 3–10 Nov — Western Pacific / around Taiwan: Taiwan's NSC said on 3 Nov that more than 100 PLAN and CCG ships were operating off Taiwan, in the South China Sea and in the Pacific. AEI/ISW link task groups from the Eastern, Northern and Southern Theater Commands, including the Liaoning carrier group, to an unannounced exercise simulating Taiwan's isolation. On 10 Nov Taiwan's defence minister called it 'area denial' drills, while Beijing has declared no exercise.

2 Nov — Sanya, Hainan: According to AEI/ISW, satellite imagery showed the carrier Fujian leaving Sanya and heading east, after at least three other major surface combatants had sortied between 26 Oct and 2 Nov.
9 Nov — Senkaku Islands: Four China Coast Guard ships entered Japanese territorial waters near Kuba Island for about two hours, the first such entry since 10 Oct (Jiji).
2, 4 and 6 Nov — Kinmen: Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration recorded CCG ships in Kinmen's restricted waters on three days in one week.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. China's own territory faces no armed threat, and its outward activity is coercive rather than hostile. That activity is nonetheless unusually large: a 100-plus-ship surge from three theatre commands beyond the first island chain, two carriers at sea, renewed Senkaku entries and steady CCG pressure on Kinmen and Pratas. Over the next 90 days, expect Beijing to keep 'quiet' unannounced surges as a normal tool, interspersed with diplomatic restraint around the APEC summit in Shenzhen and a possible Trump–Xi meeting. A named encirclement exercise remains a realistic possibility after Taiwan's 28 November local elections or in response to US arms sales. CCG 'law-enforcement patrols' east of Taiwan, at Scarborough and around the Senkakus will continue. The main risk is an unplanned collision or close air intercept with Japanese, Philippine or US forces.

countries.name: Taiwan
incidents: 2–8 Nov — Around Taiwan: The MND recorded 111 PLA aircraft sorties (78 entering the ADIZ), 53 PLAN vessel detections and 36 official ships, all up week on week, per Taiwan Security Monitor. There were median-line crossings on 2, 4 and 6 Nov and 'joint air-sea training' on 4 Nov.

10 Nov — Taipei: Defence Minister Wellington Koo confirmed China is conducting 'area denial' drills in the Western Pacific with the Liaoning carrier group, after the NSC reported more than 100 Chinese naval and coast guard ships around Taiwan and in the Pacific.

2–7 Nov — Kinmen and Pratas: The CGA recorded CCG ships in Kinmen restricted waters on 2, 4 and 6 Nov, and a CCG vessel operated near the Pratas Islands on 7 Nov. On 3 Nov the research vessel Haiyang Dizhi 8 and four Chinese fishing boats were spotted near Kaohsiung port.
6–7 Nov — Taipei: The TAIEX fell 1,873 points on 6 Nov amid the PLA surge, and the government activated its NT$500 billion National Stabilization Fund on 7 Nov.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Military pressure has risen again. The 2–8 November week had the most PLA sorties in weeks, Chinese naval and coast guard deployments around Taiwan and in the Pacific reached 100-plus ships, and CCG intrusions at Kinmen and Pratas continued, enough to move Taiwan's markets. Over the next 90 days, the run-up to the 28 November local elections and the post-APEC period are the most likely windows for a named PLA encirclement drill. Unannounced surges of 40-plus aircraft are likely to recur regardless. Expect continued CCG pressure on Kinmen and Pratas aimed at eroding Taiwan's administrative control, cognitive and election-interference operations, and diplomatic squeezes such as the closure of the PNG office. Arrivals of F-16V Block 70 jets will draw PLA responses.

forecasts.statement: The PLA Eastern Theater Command announces a named large-scale military exercise around Taiwan (in the style of Strait Thunder or Justice Mission).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by 2027-02-12, the PLA Eastern Theater Command or Chinese state media publicly announce a drill around Taiwan under a specific exercise name, as reported by Reuters, AP or Taiwan's MND. Unannounced surges and routine 'joint combat readiness patrols' do not count.

countries.name: Philippines
incidents: 3 Nov — Scarborough (Bajo de Masinloc) Shoal: The PCG said it was still assessing a Chinese vessel carrying unidentified sensor-fitted equipment inside the lagoon, whose bow and IMO numbers match no known research ship. The CCG announced 'law-enforcement patrols' at the shoal the same day.
8 Nov — Mamasapano, Maguindanao del Sur: Unidentified gunmen ambushed and killed three people, including two CAFGU active auxiliaries (Philstar).
8 Nov — Mindanao: Three soldiers were wounded in crossfire while trying to stop a clash between the Labao and Gaosil Maranao clans (Philstar).
4 Nov — Subic Bay: The US delivered T38 Devil Ray unmanned surface vessels to the Philippine Marines amid continued Chinese pressure in the South China Sea.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. No new water-cannon or collision incident was found this week, but Scarborough remains a militarised standoff. PLA combat-readiness patrols, a constant CCG and militia presence and an unidentified, possibly underwater-capable Chinese platform inside the lagoon are all in play. China's 100-plus-ship Western Pacific deployment is operating east of the archipelago, after the Liaoning transited the Basilan Strait. In Mindanao, ambushes and clan violence continue at a low level. Over the next 90 days, expect a short diplomatic lull around the ASEAN and APEC summits and Code of Conduct talks, followed by renewed CCG blocking and water-cannon use against fisheries (BFAR) and resupply missions at Scarborough, Second Thomas and Sabina Shoals. Expect PLA intercepts of PCG aircraft and more US–Philippine–Japanese maritime cooperation. A fatal incident at sea would trigger Mutual Defense Treaty consultations.

forecasts.statement: China Coast Guard vessels fire water cannon at a Philippine government vessel (PCG, BFAR or Navy) in the South China Sea.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by 2027-02-12, the PCG, the AFP or the Philippine NSC report a CCG water-cannon use against a Philippine government vessel, as carried by Reuters, AP or Philippine national media.

countries.name: South Korea
incidents: 4 Nov — East Sea: The JCS detected multiple North Korean missiles launched from Sondok, South Hamgyong, the North's fourth weapons launch in a month and its 11th suspected ballistic launch of 2026, ahead of combined ROK–US drills.

1–2 Nov — Inter-Korean border: The ROK military said it had not confirmed any operation of North Korean loudspeakers aimed at the South despite Kim Yo Jong's October deadline. North Korean MDL crossings during fortification work continue to draw warning broadcasts and warning shots, mostly on the eastern front.

10 Nov — Seoul / DMZ: Kim Yo Jong rejected the UN Secretary-General's call for dialogue and called Seoul's findings on the 21 Sep DMZ mine blast, which wounded three ROK officers, fabricated. A joint ROK–UNC investigation attributed the blast to North Korean mines.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The DMZ is the most likely point of a kinetic incident. Unresolved issues include the September mine blast, which Seoul wants an apology for and Pyongyang denies, North Korean fortification work that crosses the MDL, and a threatened but so far unconfirmed loudspeaker campaign. Missile launches toward the East Sea come several times a month. Over the next 90 days, expect more SRBM and cruise-missile launches, continued warning shots at crossing North Korean troops (though winter may slow fortification work), and Seoul continuing its talks offer while taking the mine issue to the UN. If North Korea starts sustained loudspeaker broadcasts, domestic pressure to resume South Korea's own broadcasts will grow. Watch for live fire across the MDL, further mine or drone incidents, and launches toward the NLL.

forecasts.statement: South Korean troops fire warning shots at North Korean soldiers crossing the Military Demarcation Line.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the JCS, as reported by Yonhap, Korea JoongAng Daily, Reuters or AP, confirms at least one new warning-shot incident against North Korean troops crossing the MDL between 2026-11-12 and 2027-01-31.

countries.name: Vietnam
incidents: 9 Nov — Hanoi: Vietnam and Australia held their defence policy dialogue, part of Hanoi's continued defence hedging after Indian NSA Ajit Doval's 2 Nov visit agreed co-production and maritime information-sharing.

Early Nov — Ban Keun, Laos (Vietnam's western flank): A Vietnamese official told AP that a Chinese deployment to the new Ban Keun airfield in Laos would 'naturally place a certain degree of additional military pressure on Vietnam'.
10–11 Nov — Vietnam–China border: Hanoi and Beijing agreed to strengthen coordination on border management and protection. No Vietnam–China maritime incident was found for 5–12 Nov.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. There was again no kinetic or maritime incident, but the South China Sea dispute is unchanged and Hanoi is openly worried about Chinese military access to Laos. Over the next 90 days, expect Vietnam to continue defence diplomacy with India, Australia, the US and Japan, with the Vietnam International Defence Expo in December as a showcase, while keeping party-to-party and border ties with Beijing intact. It will also continue fortifying its Spratly features. Watch for CCG harassment of Vietnamese fishermen in the Paracels, Chinese objections to Spratly construction, and any Chinese deployment to Ban Keun. A direct naval confrontation remains unlikely.

countries.name: Japan
incidents: 9 Nov — Senkaku Islands (near Kuba Island): Four China Coast Guard ships entered Japanese territorial waters and left about two hours later, the first such entry since 10 Oct (Jiji via Nippon.com).
1 Nov — Miyako Strait: According to the Joint Staff, a Chinese destroyer and a fast combat support ship transited into the Pacific, and the destroyer later returned to the East China Sea.
2 Nov — Okinawa–Miyako gap: The ASDF scrambled fighters against Chinese WZ-7 high-altitude reconnaissance drones flying from the East China Sea into the Pacific and back.

3–10 Nov — Western Pacific: More than 100 Chinese naval and coast guard ships, including the Liaoning carrier group, were deployed in clusters between Taiwan and Guam, which Taiwan calls 'area denial' drills against outside intervention.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained; watch for an upgrade. Chinese activity around Japan increased this week, with a Senkaku territorial-waters entry, warship and drone transits of the Miyako gap, and a 100-plus-ship Chinese deployment in the Western Pacific south of Japan. It stayed below the threshold of hostilities: no airspace violation, radar lock-on or missile impact in the EEZ was found. Over the next 90 days, expect more CCG entries around the Senkakus, PLAN and drone transits through the Ryukyu gaps, possible Chinese–Russian joint bomber flights, and further North Korean SRBM launches into the Sea of Japan. A close-quarters air or maritime incident, a radar lock-on like December 2025's, or a missile landing in Japan's EEZ would justify raising Japan to HIGH.

countries.name: Indonesia
incidents: 8 Nov — Camp Biru, Kali Senami, Dekai District, Yahukimo, Highland Papua: TNI troops (Satgas Rajawali V and Marines) fought a TPNPB-OPM group led by Kopitua Heluka, pushed back about 15 fighters and took their camp, seizing seven firearms. No casualties were reported.

8 Nov (report) — Papua: The Operation Damai Cartenz 2026 task force said it had arrested a suspect in the shooting death of police officer Brigpol Ronald Enok and seized seven firearms from armed groups (Metro TV).
29 Oct — Maybrat, Southwest Papua: Marines detained three alleged TPNPB-OPM members whom the military links to attacks on security posts and Trans-Bintuni road workers.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Reporting from the Papuan highlands remains sparse, and a lack of reports is not calm. Armed clashes continue, including the Yahukimo firefight and camp seizure. Police counted 29 people killed by armed groups in Highland Papua from January to September 2026, and fatal security operations hit Nduga in late October. Over the next 90 days, expect continued TNI and police operations (Habema, Damai Cartenz, Rajawali) in Yahukimo, Nduga, Intan Jaya, Puncak and Maybrat, with disputed casualty claims and displacement. TPNPB attacks on road workers, miners, aviation and alleged informants are likely to continue, especially around the 1 December 'national day'. Jakarta shows no sign of opening dialogue.

countries.name: Thailand
incidents: 9 Nov — Ban Kampong Baru, Mae Wat, Than To district, Yala: Security forces killed alleged insurgent trainer Sa-udi Ting-useng, wanted over the 2019 Lam Phaya attack that killed 15, in a dawn gunfight about 1 km from the Malaysian border during a three-day operation. Other suspects escaped.

7 Nov — Maha Wan subdistrict, Mae Sot, Tak: Artillery shells from fighting between Myanmar junta troops and resistance forces in Myawaddy Township landed in Thailand, damaging several houses without injuries.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Violence in the Deep South is intermittent but not diminished. The deadly Yala operation follows the October pipe-bomb attack in Yala, the September Sukhirin bombing and the August wave of coordinated attacks, and insurgent networks remain active along the Malaysian border. Over the next 90 days, expect sporadic ambushes, IEDs and arson in Narathiwat, Pattani and Yala, possible reprisals for the killing of Sa-udi Ting-useng, and security sweeps near the border while Bangkok reshapes the peace process. Spillover from Myanmar's fighting around Myawaddy will keep putting shells and refugees into Tak province. The Thai–Cambodian ceasefire is likely to hold. A wave of coordinated mass-casualty attacks would warrant reassessment.

countries.name: Bangladesh
incidents: 3 Nov — Joydebpur, Gazipur: Garment worker Toufiq Hossain died of injuries sustained in a clash during the minimum-wage protests, HRW said, the first confirmed death of the unrest. HRW reported police using batons and tear gas against thousands of workers.

12 Nov — Mouchak, Kaliakair, Gazipur: Workers blocked the Dhaka–Tangail highway for about three hours. Police fired sound grenades to clear it, and seven factories in the area declared a holiday (Prothom Alo).

Early Nov — Gazipur: Two garment factories were shut indefinitely after workers vandalised their premises, as protests for a Tk 30,000 minimum wage continued across Savar, Ashulia, Gazipur and Narayanganj.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The garment-wage unrest has now caused at least one confirmed death and has been running for more than a week. Highway blockades and factory closures persist despite the 1 November wage board and a January wage-hike pledge, but lethality remains limited, and political violence is factional rather than organised armed conflict. Over the next 90 days, expect recurring blockades and clashes in Gazipur, Savar and Ashulia until a new minimum wage is set, along with mob killings, intra-BNP and BNP–Jamaat clashes, and the government's framing of labour unrest as Awami League sabotage. That framing risks harsher crackdowns. An upgrade would be warranted if police fire causes multiple deaths or if the Awami League question triggers sustained street violence.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
incidents: 2 Nov — Kappalthurai, Uppuveli, Trincomalee: A gunman with a suspected T-56 rifle fired on a hired three-wheeler, killing one man (identified by police as a Navy serviceman) and wounding two. Police suspect a drug-trafficking dispute.
6 Nov — Dikwella, Matara: Police arrested the suspected gunman in the Trincomalee shooting, a former army soldier who had been formally discharged.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. Violence remains criminal: gang and narcotics-linked shootings, increasingly carried out by ex-military gunmen and now also in the Eastern Province. Police and STF operations under the anti-drug drive keep making arrests. No insurgent, terrorist or communal violence was found. Over the next 90 days, expect continued underworld shootings in the Western, Southern and Eastern provinces, police shootouts with suspects, and scrutiny of custodial deaths, with no change in the overall threat picture.

regions.name: Americas
overview: Haiti's war on the gangs moved from ground sweeps to targeted killings of leaders. Drone and helicopter-backed operations involving Haitian police, a private drone task force and Salvadoran troops killed Boston gang leader Mathias Saintil in Cite Soleil around 5–6 November. On 8 November an early-morning strike destroyed a house used by 400 Mawozo leader Wilson Joseph; he was not inside, and reports of up to 20 gunmen killed are unconfirmed. Joseph has proposed 18 November as the start of talks. The four Salvadoran technicians are still missing. Friction over command is growing: the US Embassy formally protested on 5 November that Salvadoran gunfire struck the US Embassy compound in Haiti, which El Salvador rejects, and the UN says only about 200 Salvadoran soldiers fall under the GSF.

In Colombia, attacks and bombings keep escalating each other. An explosive-drone attack on the army post at Santa Rosa del Sur (southern Bolivar) on 7 November killed three soldiers and wounded at least 16. President De la Espriella answered with his seventh bombing on 9 November ('Operation Noah' against FARC dissident Front 33 in Tibu, Catatumbo: four killed, six captured, with US MQ-9 surveillance support) and an eighth on 10 November against an unnamed 'narcoterrorist structure'. Reporting also emerged that Colombian coordinates and US drones and intelligence supported a 30 October Venezuelan strike on an ELN camp in Apure.

Emergency powers are not stopping criminal violence along the Andean–Pacific belt. Ecuador's fourth curfew of 2026 ended on 10 November after 2,292 arrests in its first week. Even so, Manabi recorded 19 killings in three days, including local journalist Tomas Beltran in Calceta on 8 November, and the 29 November local elections now follow without a curfew. In Peru, extortion attacks on transport continue: six attacks and three deaths in Lima in the week to 7 November. More than 50 bus companies suspended service for a march on Congress on 10 November, the day before Pope Leo XIV's visit began under a deployment of more than 37,000 police.

Elsewhere, pressure stayed political, humanitarian or criminal. In Venezuela, prisoner releases continue: families ended the 10-month protest camp outside El Rodeo I after Machado visited, and Foro Penal still counts 322 political prisoners. Cuba's grid deficit stays near or above half of peak demand, and the 7 November arrest of food-aid organiser Yoel Perez Serrano set off a rare street protest by mothers in El Cobre. Bolivia's announced 6 November march on La Paz drew no reported clashes, and the government on 11 November called Morales a cartel boss. The Dominican Republic keeps backing El Salvador with logistics and intelligence while describing its border as calm, and Jamaica's violence remains criminal, including more contested police killings.

countries.name: Venezuela
incidents: 30 Oct (reported 5–10 Nov) — Apure state: Venezuelan armed forces struck an ELN camp and cocaine site near the Colombian border, with US drones and intelligence according to The New York Times and with Colombian-supplied coordinates according to Cambio. Reported deaths range from about nine (La Silla Vacia) to 23 (FundaRedes); Caracas has not commented publicly.

6 Nov — El Rodeo I prison, Miranda: Maria Corina Machado visited relatives of political prisoners camped outside the prison and demanded the release of all of them. Foro Penal counts 322 political prisoners still held.

8 Nov — Caracas: Opposition negotiator Dinorah Figuera said the government will soon release a new group of political prisoners ahead of a fourth round of talks. The families dismantled the protest camp at El Rodeo I after about 10 months, and US Secretary of State Rubio urged foreign minister Oliver Blanco to continue the releases.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Within the country, the week brought no clashes with protesters, mass arrests or casualties. The political contest is running through negotiations, prisoner releases and Machado's visits, which is tension with limited violence. The 30 October Apure strike is the most significant new security fact. It is the first acknowledged-in-practice Venezuelan military action against the ELN after two decades of chavista tolerance, carried out with US support. It is still a single state-initiated strike, and there was no reported ELN retaliation or fighting on Venezuelan soil in the past seven days, so it does not yet meet the HIGH threshold. Over the next 90 days, expect more prisoner releases timed around a fourth round of talks, continued US pressure through Rubio, and Machado mobilising for an electoral timetable that the Rodriguez government is unlikely to concede quickly. The Apure precedent raises the risk of further strikes on ELN and dissident camps in Apure, Zulia and Tachira as Bogota's bombing campaign intensifies, and of ELN reprisals against Venezuelan troops. Upgrade to HIGH if strikes become repeated or the ELN hits back against Venezuelan forces, or if Machado is detained or rallies are dispersed with casualties.

forecasts.statement: Venezuela's interim government or the CNE officially announces a specific date for a presidential election.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP or EFE report that the Rodriguez government or the National Electoral Council has formally set a calendar date for a presidential election by 12 February 2027.

countries.name: Colombia
incidents: 7 Nov — Santa Rosa del Sur, Bolivar: Explosive drones struck an army post, killing three soldiers and wounding at least 16, according to the military. Local reports put the toll higher. The ELN and the Clan del Golfo operate in the area; no group has been formally named.

9 Nov — Tibu, Norte de Santander (Catatumbo): The government's seventh bombing ('Operation Noah') hit a camp of FARC dissident Front 33. Four alleged members were killed and six captured, including a commission leader close to 'Andrey Avendano', with US MQ-9 surveillance support.
10 Nov — Undisclosed location: President De la Espriella announced an eighth air strike, at 22:17, against an unnamed 'narcoterrorist structure'. No location or casualties have been released yet.
9 Nov — Choco: Fighting between the Clan del Golfo and the ELN has displaced Indigenous families as far as Medellin, with reports of kidnappings and killings.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The Santa Rosa del Sur attack, following the Planadas, Algeciras and Choco attacks of the previous week, shows armed groups killing soldiers almost weekly with explosive drones. The state now answers with air strikes every few days: two bombings in 48 hours took the total to eight in about three months. Armed groups keep effective control of parts of Catatumbo, Cauca, Choco and southern Bolivar, so the CRITICAL definition of an ongoing insurgency with regular deaths and territory held by armed groups is clearly met. Over the next 90 days, expect the bombing campaign to continue at or above the current pace against Front 33, the Mordisco and Calarca dissidents, the ELN and the Clan del Golfo, increasingly with US intelligence support and possibly cross-border coordination with Venezuela. Expect retaliation with drone, car-bomb and harassment attacks on bases and police stations, and more civilian casualties on both sides of the cycle. Drone attacks are the main killer of troops: a single attack with five or more security-force deaths is a realistic possibility. Watch the Choco ELN–Clan del Golfo war and its displacement, coca-grower protests if fumigation resumes, and any ELN reprisal for the Apure strike.

forecasts.statement: A single attack by an armed group in Colombia kills five or more soldiers and/or police officers.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, EFE or Colombian national media (El Tiempo, El Espectador) report one incident (one attack or ambush on one day) in which at least five members of the security forces were killed by an armed group, by 12 February 2027.

countries.name: Haiti
incidents: 5–6 Nov — Cite Soleil, Port-au-Prince: Boston gang leader Mathias Saintil (Viv Ansanm) was killed in a security operation that a rights group says used explosive drones. PM Fils-Aime confirmed his death. The rights group reported five gang members killed and about 15 injured in that strike.

5 Nov — Port-au-Prince: The US Embassy in San Salvador formally protested what it called poor Salvadoran coordination, alleging Salvadoran gunfire struck the US Embassy compound in Haiti and nearly hit US personnel. El Salvador rejected the claim on 9 November.

8 Nov — Near Port-au-Prince: An early-morning strike by the police drone task force, backed by contractors and Salvadoran helicopters, destroyed a house used by 400 Mawozo leader Wilson Joseph. He was not inside. Reports of up to 20 gunmen killed are unconfirmed, and rights groups and the UN have raised concerns about civilian harm.

8–10 Nov — Haiti: Wilson Joseph proposed 18 November as the start of negotiations. Rubio said El Salvador is operating separately from the international force, and the four Salvadoran technicians kidnapped on 18 October remain missing.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Gangs still control most of Port-au-Prince and large rural areas and hold foreign military personnel. State and foreign forces are now carrying out lethal drone, helicopter and ground strikes against gang leaders almost daily, which is active armed conflict and loss of state control over a significant part of the territory. The campaign has shifted to decapitation: Saintil is dead, and Joseph survived a strike on his house and is in hiding. Three separate chains of command (the GSF, the Salvadoran contingent and a contractor-supported police drone task force) raise the risk of fratricide, civilian casualties and diplomatic incidents, as the US Embassy protest showed. Over the next 90 days, expect continued strikes on 400 Mawozo, Chen Mechan and Viv Ansanm leaders in Croix-des-Bouquets, the Plaine du Cul-de-Sac and Cite Soleil, gang reprisals against civilians and possibly kidnappings, and pressure on leaders to negotiate or flee. Joseph's 18 November talks offer is unlikely to be accepted while operations are succeeding. The technicians' fate remains the main escalation trigger. Watch for civilian-casualty findings by the UN or BINUH and for any gang movement toward Kenscoff, the Artibonite or the Dominican border.

events.actor: Haitian police drone task force / Salvadoran forces

forecasts.statement: 400 Mawozo leader Wilson Joseph ('Lanmo Sanjou') is killed or taken into custody.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Haitian authorities, the Salvadoran government or the GSF confirm Joseph's death, capture or surrender, as reported by AP, Reuters, the Miami Herald or the Haitian Times, by 12 February 2027.

forecasts.statement: Haitian or Salvadoran authorities confirm the fate (found alive or confirmed dead) of the four Salvadoran aviation technicians missing since 18 October.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the Salvadoran or Haitian government officially states that the four technicians have been recovered alive or that their deaths are confirmed (identified remains included), as reported by AP, Reuters or Al Jazeera, by 31 January 2027.

countries.name: Cuba
incidents: 7 Nov — Guamuta/El Cobre, Santiago de Cuba: Special forces and State Security raided the home of Yoel Alejandro Perez Serrano, who runs a free-meals project for more than 400 people, and detained him. Dozens of residents, including mothers with small children, marched through El Cobre demanding his release. His wife and some protesters were reportedly detained.

8–9 Nov — El Cobre: Food trucks appeared in El Cobre and Guamuta the day after the protest. As of 9 November, Perez Serrano had not been released and authorities had not disclosed where he is held or any charges.
4 Nov — Nationwide: The Electric Union forecast 960 MW available against peak demand of 2,850 MW, a generation deficit of about 1,890 MW with seven thermal units out of service.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Basic services remain in collapse, with peak-hour generation covering roughly a third to a half of demand. Repression continues, and the El Cobre episode shows the pattern the previous COA anticipated: a targeted arrest set off a local street protest, which the state answered with detentions and an ad hoc food delivery rather than lethal force. Over the next 90 days, expect at least one further total or partial collapse of the national grid. Four total disconnections had already occurred by July 2026. Expect also recurring pot-banging and small street protests in eastern provinces and Havana, met with short detentions, Decree-Law 370 fines and internet or phone cuts. Political-prisoner numbers (about 680 per Cubalex) and US–Cuba friction will persist. Upgrade to CRITICAL only if protests coordinate across several cities, security forces use lethal force, or state control visibly erodes.

forecasts.statement: Cuba's national electric system (SEN) suffers a total nationwide disconnection (complete grid collapse).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the Ministry of Energy and Mines or the UNE announces a total disconnection of the SEN, as reported by EFE, Reuters, AP or 14ymedio, by 12 February 2027. Partial or regional collapses do not count.

countries.name: Ecuador
incidents: 7–8 Nov — Manabi: Primicias reported 19 killings in three days across Montecristi, Manta, Bolivar, Portoviejo, Sucre, El Carmen, Pedernales and Jipijapa, including three people shot dead in Calceta on 7 November and two men killed in a house in Montecristi on 8 November. Manabi has recorded 1,018 violent deaths in 2026.

8 Nov — Calceta, Manabi: Local news-page journalist Tomas Beltran was shot dead outside his home. He had reported death threats and was in the prosecutor's witness-protection system; the Inter American Press Association condemned the killing.
9 Nov — Guayaquil (via a la Costa km 22): Gunmen attacked a pickup truck at the entrance to a residential development, killing two women.

8–10 Nov — Guayas, Manabi, Los Rios, El Oro, Esmeraldas: The Interior Ministry reported 2,292 people captured in the curfew's first week, with 204 firearms and 612 kg of drugs seized. The fourth curfew of 2026 ended at 05:00 on 10 November, ahead of the 29 November local elections.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Even under a curfew with thousands of arrests, Manabi recorded 19 killings in three days, a journalist under protection was assassinated, and killings continued in Guayaquil. Ecuador's organised violence remains large-scale, with regular deaths, and the state still frames it as an 'internal armed conflict'. With the curfew lifted on 10 November, expect night-time killings to rebound, as after the March and September curfews. The 29 November local elections are the main near-term risk: attacks on candidates, local officials or journalists are plausible in Manabi, Guayas, Los Rios and El Oro. Over the 90-day horizon, expect renewal of the state of exception, further military-police sweeps against Los Lobos, Los Choneros and Los Lagartos, continued prison killings after the late-October massacres in Latacunga and El Inca, and a fifth curfew if killings spike again, which is likely given the government's pattern of reissuing them.

events.place: Guayas, Manabi, Los Rios, El Oro, Esmeraldas

forecasts.statement: President Noboa decrees a fifth curfew of 2026–27 covering at least one coastal province (Guayas, Manabi, Los Rios, El Oro or Esmeraldas).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if an executive decree imposing a new night-time curfew in at least one of these provinces takes effect after 12 November 2026, as reported by Primicias, El Universo, EFE or Reuters, by 12 February 2027.

countries.name: Peru
incidents: Week to 7 Nov — Lima/Callao: America TV counted six extortion attacks on public transport and three deaths in a week, in districts including San Juan de Lurigancho, Callao, Villa El Salvador, Surquillo, Carabayllo and Chorrillos, including bus driver Josue Perdomo Estrada, shot six times in Chorrillos. The Public Ministry recorded 169 extortion attacks on transport companies (95 dead) between January and October 2026.

10 Nov — Lima: More than 50 public transport companies suspended service for a march from Plaza de Acho to Congress against extortion and driver killings, threatening a strike if the government does not act. Heavy-cargo hauliers separately announced a 72-hour national strike for 16–18 November over diesel prices.

11 Nov — Lima/Callao: Pope Leo XIV's visit began under a security plan of more than 37,000 police nationwide (22,464 in Lima and Callao) and drone-flight restrictions in six cities through 16 November.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Extortion gangs keep killing transport workers every week in Lima and Callao despite repeated emergency extensions. October was the most violent month of the year for attacks on transport. This is recurring lethal violence by organised criminal groups, while the state keeps territorial control. The papal visit (to 16–17 November) will saturate Lima, Chiclayo, Cusco and Pucallpa with police and may temporarily push attacks to outer districts. Over the next 90 days, expect continued driver and mototaxi killings, recurring transport stoppages and marches (the 10 November action and the 16–18 November cargo strike are early signs), more arrests of extortion cells, and government pressure for tougher anti-extortion legislation. A citywide public-transport strike in Lima/Callao after a high-profile killing is likely. Upgrade triggers: a mass-casualty attack on a bus, attacks on officials or on the papal programme, or violent clashes during transport strikes.

forecasts.statement: Public transport unions in Lima/Callao carry out a strike (paro) against extortion in which a majority of formal bus companies suspend service for at least one day.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Peruvian national media (El Comercio, La Republica, RPP, Infobae Peru) or Reuters/AP report a transport strike in Lima/Callao described as widespread or as paralysing most routes, held after 12 November 2026 and by 12 February 2027.

countries.name: Bolivia
incidents: 6–7 Nov — Patacamaya/La Paz: Police deployed 450 officers to control Patacamaya and eight entry points to La Paz ahead of the Morales-aligned march called for 6 November. Police reported no irregularities and normal traffic, and no blockades or clashes were reported.

11 Nov — La Paz: Government Minister Marco Antonio Oviedo called Evo Morales 'the chief of a cartel' trafficking drugs from the Chapare (Tropico de Cochabamba). He said police detected more than 8 million bolivianos moving from the Tropico to finance the May–June blockades, which left 16 dead.

12 Nov — La Paz: Defence Minister Ernesto Justiniano said the armed forces are being prepared to confront 'narcoterrorism' in support of, not in place of, the police, citing lessons from the 53-day crisis.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The announced 6 November march on La Paz produced no reported blockades, clashes or casualties, which confirms the weak mobilising capacity of Morales' camp after the October postponements. The situation remains political tension with limited violence. The government is now escalating rhetorically and legally, labelling Morales a cartel boss and preparing the armed forces for a counter-narcotics role, on top of existing terrorism and trafficking warrants. This raises the medium-term risk of a confrontation in the Chapare, where supporters guard Morales around the clock. Over the next 90 days, expect intermittent, mostly contained marches and blockade attempts, COB pressure over fuel and food prices, and continued use of the state of exception (to 17 December) and its possible renewal. Upgrade to HIGH if a police or military operation to arrest Morales in the Chapare triggers armed resistance, if multi-day blockades on main highways resume, or if clearances cause deaths.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
incidents: 10 Nov — Santo Domingo: President Abinader confirmed that the Dominican Republic provides logistics and intelligence to Salvadoran forces fighting gangs in Haiti and urged better coordination between them and the GSF. He said the southern border has been reinforced and gang activity remains concentrated in and around Port-au-Prince.

4 Nov — Dajabon, Elias Pina, Jimani, Pedernales: The Defence Minister toured four crossings and called the border 'totally calm'. About 11,000 troops are deployed along the frontier, and the government says it could close the border if needed.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. There was no organised armed or political violence on Dominican territory. The border build-up is defensive, and the president says gang activity stays concentrated around Port-au-Prince. Over the next 90 days, the shift in Haiti toward drone strikes on gang leaders in Croix-des-Bouquets and the Plaine du Cul-de-Sac, about 45 km from Jimani, is the main external risk: it could push fleeing gang members or displaced civilians toward the frontier. Santo Domingo's openly declared intelligence and logistics role for El Salvador could make Dominican interests a rhetorical or actual target for Viv Ansanm. Expect continued reinforcements, mass deportations and possible temporary crossing closures if fighting moves east. Upgrade to MODERATE if gang fighting crosses the border, Dominican forces engage armed groups, or cross-border incidents cause casualties.

countries.name: Jamaica
incidents: 8 Nov — St Elizabeth (Monymusk and Williamsfield areas): In predawn operations, security forces fatally shot two murder suspects, Dadrian White and Oshane Wright, in two separate 'alleged confrontations' about 45 minutes apart. Police say two firearms were recovered.
4 Nov — St Elizabeth: A man was fatally shot by a licensed firearm holder at a bar.
3 Nov — Manchester: Police said a man killed in a firefight with officers was on his way to carry out a contract killing, the third police killing in Manchester and St Catherine in about a week.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. Violence remains individual criminal shootings and contested police killings, not organised political or armed-group violence, and national murder figures remain on track for a historic low. The main concern is still the high rate of fatal police shootings. Two more men were killed in St Elizabeth on 8 November, bringing police killings in the south-central parishes to at least five in about ten days, which will feed INDECOM probes and community distrust. Over the next 90 days, expect continued contested police shootings, roadblock protests after disputed killings, contract killings in Manchester and St Elizabeth, and the usual rise in criminal violence in December. Upgrade to MODERATE only if planned ambushes on police, sustained unrest in Kingston, St Andrew or St Catherine, or a sharp rise in gang feuds emerges.
